title: plantago coronopus subsp. ceratophylla
intro: Plantago coronopus subsp. ceratophylla, commonly known as Buck's-hoary plantain, is a subspecies of the plantain family (Plantaginaceae) that is native to the Mediterranean region. The plant is valued for its potential health benefits, including its ability to aid in wound healing, reduce inflammation, and exhibit antimicrobial properties. The therapeutic actions of Plantago coronopus subsp. ceratophylla are attributed to its bioactive constituents, which include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids. These bioactive compounds may contribute to the plant's ability to exhibit antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antiviral activities.
